# Station Safety In the less-than-civilized reaches of Fringe Space, danger is everywhere—and it's often wrought by fellow crew members. Most prominently, rival groups within the Syndicate are known to supply covert agents with the tools necessary to infiltrate allied stations for their own gain.
But out in spaces like this, the Syndicate has far fewer resources to spare. [color=red]Stations like yours have no standing security force,[/color] save for a lone [color=#1b67a5]Escort[/color] charged with the protection of Command staff.
That means you'll need to stay vigilant to keep yourself and the rest of your crew safe, and possibly get your hands dirty when things start going down. To that end, this section of the guidebook will describe the resources available to fringe Syndicate stations for preserving safety in dire times.
## Levels of Responsibility [color=yellow]Fringe Space is not bound by the tenets of Space Law.[/color] Punishments for offenses against the station (and, indeed, what counts as an offense to begin with) is left for the crew to figure out, under the guidance of Command.
That being said, the crew is encouraged to remember the difference between a threat to the station and a threat to its corporate operations.
Cases like theft, trespassing, and interpersonal assault are not something your employers generally concern themselves with—those are issues for you to solve as a station, and can be handled with non-lethal arrest and probation as the crew sees fit.
But threats to the bottom line and/or operations greater in scope than your station, such as uprisings or acts of corporate espionage, have a greater sense of responsibility attached. In these situations, it is expected that the crew will do what they can to ensure that the threat is handled by the end of their shift.
If nothing else, remember: It's your paycheck on the line.
## Handling Criminals The tools accessible when the station is threatened are elaborated on in the [textlink="Armory" link="Armory"] section of the guidebook, and focus on subdual and surveillance.
For those who are deemed a true danger to Syndicate operations, it is recommended to simply confiscate any illegal possessions found and keep a very close eye on them. After the shift, they can be brought to Central Command and taken in by corporate security.
The matter of how a criminal is meant to be watched and prevented from doing additional harm without a police force or a brig is left for the crew to figure out. Your employers at the Syndicate suggest finding a way to ensure the criminal can continue their work, perhaps under direct surveillance by a capable volunteer. You still have quotas to reach, after all.
## Holding Cell On every station, there will be a heavily reinforced unit meant to contain threats that cannot be subdued through normal means. Monsters, highly dangerous eldritch artifacts, killer robots, and other inhuman threats can be kept here while the rest of the crew forms a plan.
[color=red]Do not mistake a holding cell for a brig.[/color] It is little more than a metal box with a control panel for operating its blast doors and shutters. Unlike a holding cell, there is no way for those on either side of the walls to interact with each other. Additionally, as a public utility, the holding cell is available to all members of the crew.
